title: Essay Writing
description: Structuring arguments clearly with introduction, body, and conclusion.

notes.heading: Essay Structure
notes.body: Introduction → Body paragraphs → Conclusion. Introduction grabs attention, gives background, ends with thesis statement. Each body paragraph develops one point with evidence and analysis. Conclusion summarises and leaves a final thought.

notes.heading: The Thesis Statement
notes.body: A single sentence at the end of your introduction stating your main argument. Must be specific and debatable. Example: "In Macbeth, Shakespeare shows that unchecked ambition leads to self-destruction."

notes.heading: PEEL Paragraph Method
notes.body: P=Point (main idea), E=Evidence (quote/fact), E=Explanation (how evidence proves your point), L=Link (connect back to thesis or to next paragraph).

flashcards.definition: A clear, specific sentence stating the essay's main argument.
Paragraph structure: Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link.
Opening sentence of a body paragraph stating its main idea.
Final paragraph summarising the argument and providing a closing thought.
Words linking ideas: Furthermore, however, in contrast, as a result.

questions.stem: Where does the thesis statement typically appear?
questions.explanation: Usually at the end of the introduction.

questions.stem: In PEEL, what does the second E stand for?

choices: "Zoos should be banned because they prioritise entertainment over animal welfare."
Some people think zoos are bad.
questions.explanation: Specific and debatable — makes a clear claim with a reason.

questions.stem: A topic sentence's purpose is to:
questions.explanation: Topic sentences focus the paragraph on one idea.
"However" signals a contrast or shift in argument.
